profile.title: Pi host foundation — Ubuntu Server 24.04 ARM64

target.device: Raspberry Pi sensor VM / hardware target

modules.title: Ubuntu host baseline
modules.summary: Verify OS image, systemd, package tools, time synchronization, storage, recovery console, and a non-root administrator.

modules.title: Host-side package prerequisites
modules.summary: Audit CA certificates, curl, git, Python 3 and venv support; do not add application, database, or build-only packages by assumption.

modules.title: ZeroTier management network prerequisite
modules.summary: Validate the ZeroTier ARM64 client and service on the VM; network ID, membership authorization, and credentials remain operator-controlled and are not joined during the clean-image check.

modules.title: Service identity and filesystem layout contract
modules.summary: Specify non-login service identities, protected configuration paths, release/current layout, writable state, and read-only Cowrie/Zeek log access without installing services.

host_dependencies.reason: Required to manage and inspect a native Ubuntu Server guest; the preflight checks presence without changing the host.
Candidate tools for validating and retrieving pinned artifacts; package state and source policy must be checked on the clean VM.
Current Cowrie documentation lists Python 3.10+ and virtualenv; verify the project's pinned 2.6.1-derived revision before locking the Ubuntu package mapping.

items: snapd only if the Snap method is approved
host_dependencies.reason: The official Snap is an ARM64-capable candidate but refresh behavior and the actual service/interface contract need VM validation; do not join a production network as part of the image test.
The six Go agents were built as statically linked Linux ARM64 binaries. Keep the Go toolchain and module cache on the controlled build host.

The pinned Cowrie runtime and Zeek ARM64 package/interface strategy must be tested after the clean host baseline. The tracked Zeek unit currently assumes /usr/local/zeek while the official binary-package instructions use /opt/zeek.
Database and web deployment are intentionally outside the current Pi host-foundation work.

package_audit.scope_note: Candidate packages only. This read-only audit inspects the local dpkg status database; it never runs apt update/install or resolves package versions/origins.

separate_targets.title: Full Pi sensor installation plan
separate_targets.reason: The complete sensor/data/web plan remains documented separately and is not part of the current host-foundation phase.

separate_targets.title: GCP dashboard and post-session analysis
separate_targets.reason: Separate host, identity, credentials, and deployment lifecycle; do not install these services on the Pi profile.

blockers: Qualify the exact Ubuntu Server 24.04 ARM64 image build and supported Raspberry Pi model on the external clean VM/hardware target.
Audit the candidate Ubuntu package set against the clean image before adding packages; do not run an OS-wide upgrade as part of preflight.
Select and test the ZeroTier ARM64 package method and refresh policy; keep membership identity and network ID outside Git and this profile.
Resolve the per-service account/group/ACL matrix for Cowrie and Zeek logs before writing portable systemd units.
